text: A built-in check that owns internal/factory or internal/plumbing gets half an hour, 25 minutes of it for its tests, beside internal/verify's hour with 55 (#487). It replaces D-0504, whose arithmetic for internal/plumbing was wrong. The budgets are one table of exact packages, and a check gets the longest among those it selects; every other package keeps ten minutes inside twelve. Measured on 11-19 in the pinned sandbox image, at four CPUs with a cold cache: internal/factory's test binary compiled in 30 seconds, then dashboard's in 4, formalize's in 1.4, verify's in 6.4, and go vet ./... ran in 18. The slowest tests took 87 seconds alone in factory, 24 in dashboard and 65 for a verify Python application test. With no other sandbox, a whole check of formalize, factory and dashboard took 3 minutes 16 seconds, factory's 429 tests 7.9 minutes of test time among them; beside three other sandboxes it didn't finish in twelve. internal/plumbing's tests took 58.5 minutes of test time in a build on 11-13, at least 7.3 minutes at eight workers. 25 minutes is that whole check slowed sevenfold, and plumbing's tests slowed threefold. On the host with a warm cache, go test -count=1 -run '^$' ./internal/factory/ took 3.1 seconds. A direct build that owns either package asks for 31 minutes 15 seconds of tool time. A planner's check tool asks for the longest built-in check, 61 minutes 15 seconds, since the plan, and so the budget its check selects, doesn't exist when the agent starts.
